rows.text: Back Skellefteå AIK on the moneyline when Djurgårdens IF visit Skellefteå Kraft Arena on Thursday. The official SHL table has Skellefteå third on 19 points from ten games (5-3-2, 32 goals for and 25 against) and 3-1-1 at home, while Djurgården are 12th on 12 points after eleven games with 23 scored and 33 conceded, and they are winless in five away games (0-2-3). Skellefteå have won three of their last five, and our goal-grid model makes them a 71.0% shot at 1.41 fair decimal (-244 American).

Back Minnesota Wild on the moneyline at Scotiabank Saddledome on Thursday. Minnesota are 6-2-2 with 14 points, 31 goals for and 25 against, and Kirill Kaprizov leads the NHL with eleven goals while Quinn Hughes has eleven assists from defence; both figures are confirmed on the NHL's official 2026-27 leaders feed. Calgary are 2-6-0 with only 17 goals scored and 37 conceded, and their 1-3-0 home record includes being outscored 19-9. Our shrunk Poisson model prices the Wild at 70.8% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Carolina Hurricanes +1.5 on the puck line at Rogers Place on Thursday. Carolina are 8-2-1 with 42 goals for and 27 against, and their 17 points lead the Eastern Conference; Edmonton are 7-1-1 with 41 scored and 27 conceded, both records confirmed on the NHL's official standings page. The leaders feed shows Connor McDavid on twenty assists and Leon Draisaitl on eight goals, so Edmonton's threat is real. The +1.5 cover cashes on any Carolina win or one-goal defeat, including overtime, and our Poisson grid prices it at 70.3% (1.42 fair decimal, -238).

Back Boston Bruins on the moneyline when the San Jose Sharks visit TD Garden on Saturday, 24 October. Boston are 7-2-1 with 36 goals for and 22 against after ten games, and Jeremy Swayman is 6-1-1 with a 1.98 goals-against average and a .928 save percentage; David Pastrnak had six points through those ten games. San Jose opened its road trip in Ottawa on 22 October. Our shrunk Poisson model makes Boston a 71.1% favourite at 1.41 fair decimal (-244 American).

Take Minnesota Wild +1.5 on the handicap at Delta Center on Tuesday, 27 October. Minnesota arrive 6-2-2 with 31 goals for and 25 against, and Kirill Kaprizov's eleven goals plus Quinn Hughes's eleven assists are both confirmed on the NHL's official leaders feed. Utah are 7-3-0 with 38 goals scored, and Nick Schmaltz has seven goals. The +1.5 cushion covers a one-goal defeat, including overtime, and our goal-grid model grades it at 70.6% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Buffalo Sabres +1.5 on the handicap at SAP Center on Tuesday. Buffalo are 4-4-2 through ten games with 28 goals for and 36 against, and they have taken points in six of those ten. San Jose are 5-4-1 and have conceded 34 goals in ten. Tage Thompson's five goals lead the Sabres' attack, while Macklin Celebrini has five goals and nine assists for the Sharks. The model's central projection is a one-goal game, so the +1.5 cushion prices at 71.1% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Toronto Maple Leafs +1.5 at Climate Pledge Arena on Wednesday, 28 October. Toronto are 5-4-2 with 38 goals for and 34 against, and Auston Matthews has eight goals and ten assists for 18 points, confirmed on the NHL's official leaders feed. Seattle are 6-3-1 with 37 scored and 34 conceded. The model projects 7.09 combined goals, and with the Leafs' attack capable of keeping any game inside a goal, the half-goal cushion grades at 70.3% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Washington Capitals +1.5 at Bridgestone Arena on Thursday, 29 October. Washington are 5-4-0 with 30 goals for and 29 against. Nashville are 3-2-3 after eight games with 23 scored and 22 conceded, and they have needed extra time three times. Roman Josi has six assists, Ryan O'Reilly four goals and Juuse Saros three wins, all confirmed on the NHL's official game page. The model makes a one-goal game the central outcome, pricing Washington +1.5 at 70.9% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Pittsburgh Penguins +1.5 at the Bell Centre on Saturday, 31 October. Pittsburgh are 3-6-1 with 32 goals for and 37 against, and Erik Karlsson's ten assists are confirmed on the NHL's official leaders feed. Montreal are 4-3-2 with 28 scored and 34 conceded, and Cole Caufield has six goals while Nick Suzuki has seven assists. Neither side has blown opponents out, so a Penguins defeat by two or more is the outlier; the +1.5 grades at 70.5% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Colorado Avalanche on the moneyline at United Center on Monday, 2 November. Colorado are 5-4-1 with 41 goals scored and 30 conceded, and Nathan MacKinnon's ten assists plus Artturi Lehkonen's eight goals are both confirmed on the NHL's official leaders feed. Chicago are 3-6-0 with 21 scored and 36 conceded through nine games. Our normal-margin model makes the visitors a 70.2% shot at 1.42 fair decimal (-238 American).

Back Stade Aurillacois on the 1X2 line to beat USON Nevers in Pro D2 round eight. Aurillac have won their last two, against Biarritz and Béziers, to reach 16 points with a 3-0-4 record and 240 points scored. Nevers are winless in seven (0-0-7) with 146 scored and 222 conceded, and the official LNR table confirms they are last. Our margin model prices the home win at 70.5% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Connacht Rugby on the 1X2 line to beat Zebre Parma at Dexcom Stadium on Friday. Connacht are 1-0-2 with 56 points for and 84 against, while Zebre are bottom of the URC at 0-0-3 with 52 scored and 116 conceded after a 29-12 home defeat to Edinburgh. The official URC table confirms the gap between the sides, and our shrunk margin model prices the Galway win at 70.3% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Take Luca Van Assche +1.5 sets against Valentin Vacherot in Thursday's round-of-16 tie on the indoor hard courts. The ATP list captured for this desk has Vacherot at #32 on 1,480 points and Van Assche at #48 on 1,065, a gap of 415 points rather than a gulf, and the set handicap gives the lower-ranked Belgian room to lose a tight match and still cover. Our best-of-three set model gives Van Assche a 71.3% chance of covering +1.5 sets, priced at 1.40 fair decimal (-250 American).

Back Arthur Fils on the moneyline against Adrian Mannarino in Thursday evening's all-French round-of-16 tie in Brussels. The captured ATP list has Fils at #10 on 3,325 points and Mannarino at #79 on 743, and the indoor hard court rewards Fils's heavier serve and first-strike return. Our best-of-three model makes Fils a 70.8% favourite at 1.41 fair decimal (-243 American), with the set line offering the safer route if the veteran keeps the first set close.

Back Philadelphia 76ers on the moneyline when Milwaukee Bucks visit Xfinity Mobile Arena on Saturday, 24 October. The official game page carries Philadelphia's 2025-26 finish at 45-37 with a 23-18 home record, against Milwaukee's 32-50 season and a 13-28 road mark. Opening-week rosters can shift the picture, but the baseline gap is 13 wins and a home court that held up last season. Our margin model makes the 76ers a 70.1% shot at 1.43 fair decimal (-233 American).

Take Milwaukee Bucks at home against Indiana Pacers on Monday, 26 October. Milwaukee's 2025-26 line was 32-50 overall but 19-22 at Fiserv Forum, while Indiana finished 19-63 and won only eight road games all season (8-33), per the official game page. That is the weakest travelling profile in the sample, and the model prices a Bucks win at 71.6% (1.40 fair decimal, -250 American).

Back Houston Rockets on the moneyline at American Airlines Center on Friday, 30 October. The official game page records Houston at 52-30 last season with a 22-19 road record, while Dallas went 26-56 and 16-25 at home. A 26-win gap is the largest on this NBA card, and the Emirates NBA Cup setting does not change the talent baseline. Our model gives Houston 70.8% at 1.41 fair decimal (-244 American).

Take San Antonio Spurs at Frost Bank Center on Saturday, 31 October. San Antonio closed 2025-26 at 62-20 with a 32-8 home record, the best home mark in this set, while Minnesota were 49-33 and 23-18 on the road, per the official game page. The Spurs' home edge is worth roughly seven points in our margin model, which prices them at 71.4% (1.40 fair decimal, -250 American).

Back Tommy Paul to beat Corentin Moutet in Friday's quarter-final in Vienna. The captured ATP list has Paul at #15 on 2,575 points and Moutet at #94 on 640, and Paul's footspeed and flat backhand give him the edge on an indoor hard court against a left-handed counterpuncher. Our best-of-three binomial model prices the American at 71.6% (1.40 fair decimal, -250 American), just inside the brief's short-price limit.

Back Minnesota Wild (Moneyline) at Scotiabank Saddledome on Thursday night. Minnesota have banked 14 points from ten games (6-2-2) on the back of just 25 goals conceded (2.50 per game), while Calgary sit 2-6-0 having scored only 17 goals in eight outings and shipped 37. Our shrunk Poisson model makes the visiting Wild a 70.8% shot (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Carolina Hurricanes +1.5 (Handicap) in Thursday's heavyweight clash at Rogers Place. Carolina have lost only twice in regulation through eleven games (8-2-1, 17 points, 42 scored against 27 allowed), a profile built on one-goal games, while Edmonton (7-1-1, 41-27) rarely blow elite opponents away. The +1.5 puck line cashes on any Hurricanes win or one-goal defeat including overtime, and our Poisson grid prices that cover at 70.3% (1.42, -238 American).

Back Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens -5.75 (Alternate Handicap) in EuroLeague Round 7 at Telekom Center Athens rather than swallowing the ultra-short straight moneyline. Panathinaikos sit top of the 20-club standings at 5-1 with a competition-best +90 point differential (528 scored, 438 conceded) and a 4-1 home record. Baskonia arrive bottom at 1-5 (-60 differential, 0-2 away, allowing 94.0 points per game), so covering a reduced spread prices at 71.0% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Stade Toulousain -3.25 (Alternate Handicap) against USA Perpignan on Saturday afternoon in Top 14 Journée 7. Toulouse sit first on 24 points (5W-0D-1L, 197 for, 124 against, +73) riding five consecutive league wins plus a 60-14 Champions Cup demolition of Sale Sharks. Ninth-placed Perpignan (3W-0D-3L, 166-199, -33) must keep it within a converted score to spoil a 70.6% cover price (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Provence Rugby -5.25 (Alternate Handicap) against AS Béziers Hérault in Friday's Pro D2 Journée 8 card. Unbeaten Provence stand 7W-0D-0L on 29 points after conceding just 158 points across seven rounds (222 scored, +64). Fourteenth-placed Béziers have lost three of their last five matches while shipping 240 points (-93 differential), and covering a one-score alternate line rates 70.5% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Stade Aurillacois (1X2 Match Winner) — Stade Aurillacois simply to beat USON Nevers at home in Pro D2 Journée 8. Aurillac arrive on back-to-back victories over Biarritz and Béziers to reach 16 points (3W-0D-4L, 240 points scored). Bottom-placed Nevers are the lone winless club in the division at 0W-0D-7L with a -76 differential (146 scored, 222 conceded), putting the home win at 70.5% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Connacht Rugby (1X2 Match Winner) — Connacht Rugby to defeat Zebre Parma at Dexcom Stadium in Friday's URC Round 4 meeting. Bottom-placed Zebre arrive at 0W-0D-3L with a competition-worst -64 differential (52 scored, 116 conceded) after losing 29-12 to Edinburgh on 10 October. Against 1W-0D-2L Connacht (56 PF, 84 PA) in Galway, our shrunk margin model prices the home win at 70.2% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Take Edinburgh Rugby -1.75 (Alternate Handicap) at home against 10bet Lions in Friday night's URC Round 4 fixture rather than the short outright price. Edinburgh sit top of the URC on 14 points as the only 3W-0D-0L side (80 PF, 54 PA) after beating Zebre 29-12 away, whereas the Lions shipped 57 points at Loftus last time out (77 PF, 102 PA overall). Winning by two or more rates 70.2% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Vodacom Bulls -3.75 (Alternate Handicap) against Ulster Rugby at Loftus Versfeld on Saturday morning in URC Round 4. Pretoria's Bulls lead the entire URC in scoring with 126 points across three matches against only 54 conceded (+72), fresh off hammering the Lions 57-15 on 10 October. Winless Ulster enter at 0W-2D-1L (88 PF, 93 PA), and a four-point winning margin prices at 70.7% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take DHL Stormers -0.75 (Alternate Handicap) at DHL Stadium in Saturday's URC Round 4 clash with the Scarlets. Cape Town's Stormers stand 4th on 11 points (2W-0D-1L, 81 PF, joint-best 54 PA) coming off a comprehensive 39-22 home victory over the Sharks on 10 October. Twelfth-placed Scarlets sit 1W-0D-2L (-17 differential, 68 PF, 85 PA), making any home win beyond a penalty a 71.4% cover (1.40 fair decimal, -250 American).

Back Glasgow Warriors -1.25 (Alternate Handicap) in Friday night's URC Round 5 clash with 10bet Lions at Scotstoun Stadium. Unbeaten Glasgow sit second on 13 points (2W-1D-0L, 95 points scored, 72 conceded) after beating Connacht 36-19 at home on 9 October. Seventh-placed Lions have shipped 102 points in three games following their 57-15 loss in Pretoria, so a two-point home margin rates 70.9% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Back Vodacom Bulls -4.75 (Alternate Handicap) at Loftus Versfeld in Saturday's URC Round 5 fixture against the Scarlets. Pretoria's Bulls lead the URC with 126 points scored and only 54 allowed (+72) after their 57-15 demolition of the Lions, while twelfth-placed Scarlets sit 1W-0D-2L (-17 differential, 68 PF, 85 PA). Clearing a five-point alternate spread prices the hosts at 70.7% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Take Dragons RFC -3.25 (Alternate Handicap) at Rodney Parade against Zebre Parma in Saturday's URC Round 5 meeting. Eighth-placed Dragons hold a +5 differential on 9 points (1W-1D-1L, 88 PF, 83 PA) after scoring 31 points at home on 9 October, whereas bottom-placed Zebre are 0W-0D-3L with a competition-worst -64 differential (52 PF, 116 PA). Winning by four or more rates 70.2% (1.42 fair decimal, -238 American).

Back Barça -3.5 (Alternate Handicap) at Palau Blaugrana in Thursday's EHF Champions League Group E clash instead of the prohibitive 1X2 price. Barça have won all four group fixtures (4W-0D-0L, 8 points) while conceding only 104 goals — the stingiest mark among all 24 clubs — alongside 137 goals scored. Against 1W-0D-3L Montpellier (116 GF, 125 GA), winning by four or more projects at 70.7% (1.41 fair decimal, -244 American).

Back North Melbourne Tasmanian Kangaroos -13.5 pts at -227 (1.44 fair decimal, 69.5% model probability) at Arden Street Oval. North Melbourne sit atop the official NAB AFLW Round 10 ladder on 36 premiership points with an extraordinary 251.9% scoring percentage, driven by midfielders Jasmine Garner and Ash Riddell. Seventh-placed Adelaide arrive at 24 points (105.7%), making the standard half-point handicap far cleaner than North's sub--250 moneyline chalk.

Take Geelong Cats -2.5 pts at -238 (1.42 fair decimal, 70.6% model probability) at GMHBA Stadium in Geelong. Second-placed Geelong hold 36 premiership points and a 167.2% percentage through ten completed rounds behind on-ballers Georgie Prespakis and Nina Morrison, giving the Cats genuine home-ground separation against fourth-placed Brisbane (28 points, 149.1%) without paying unplayable heavy-chalk juice.

Play Milwaukee Brewers to Win at -161 (1.62 fair decimal, 61.7% model probability) in Game 1 of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field. Milwaukee posted MLB's best record at 103-59 (832 runs scored, 618 allowed) and just swept the Dodgers 4-0 in the NLCS behind Jackson Chourio (25 homers, .291 average), Brice Turang (100 RBIs), and flamethrower Jacob Misiorowski (1.80 ERA). Even against Junior Caminero's 42-homer Tampa Bay lineup, Milwaukee's +128-run differential edge over the 98-64 Rays makes the home opener an elite in-band play.

Stick with Milwaukee Brewers to Win at -161 (1.62 fair decimal, 61.7% model probability) for Saturday night's World Series Game 2 in Milwaukee. Catcher William Contreras (18 home runs, 94 RBIs) and first baseman Jake Bauers (team-high 26 homers) anchor an offense that outscored opponents by 214 runs over 162 games before outscoring Los Angeles 21-11 in a four-game NLCS sweep, while Tampa Bay went 43-38 on the road despite Drew Rasmussen's 2.67 ERA.

Kendrick Nunn and Kostas Sloukas have turned OAKA Altion into Europe's toughest floor, making Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens -12.5 pts at -227 (1.44 fair decimal, 69.5% model probability) the sharpest EuroLeague Round 7 position. Panathinaikos lead all 20 clubs at 5-1 with a +90 scoring differential (528 scored, 438 conceded) and a 4-1 home record, whereas 19th-placed Kosner Baskonia sit 1-5 (-60 differential, 0-3 away).

Valencia Basket's 90.0-point EuroLeague offense sets up Valencia Basket to Win at -222 (1.45 fair decimal, 68.8% model probability) inside Adidas Arena on Thursday night. Guard Jean Montero and forward Semi Ojeleye have propelled fifth-placed Valencia to a 4-2 record and +46 margin (540 PF, 494 PA), facing an 18th-placed Paris Basketball defense that has dropped five of six games (1-5, 488:546) while yielding 91.0 points per outing.

Lay Oklahoma City Thunder -0.5 pts at -238 (1.42 fair decimal, 70.5% model probability) as Oklahoma City host Nikola Jokić and the Denver Nuggets at Paycom Center. Two-time reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander poured in 32 points alongside Chet Holmgren to beat San Antonio 108-100 in Tuesday's October 20 season opener, building directly on a 64-18 campaign in which the Thunder went 34-7 on their home floor while trimming OKC's -256 moneyline chalk inside our focus band.

Back India to Win at -167 (1.60 fair decimal, 62.6% model probability) in Thursday's 1st T20I at Hagley Oval, Christchurch. Stand-in skipper Shreyas Iyer leads an Indian squad stacked with T20 World Cup winners Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson, Kuldeep Yadav, and Arshdeep Singh, entering at #1 on the ICC T20I table (272 rating) after crushing Mitchell Santner's Black Caps 255/5 to 159 in the March 2026 World Cup Final.

Play Afghanistan -16.5 runs-eq at -233 (1.43 fair decimal, 70.2% model probability) in Friday's UAE ODI Tri-Series Final at Sheikh Zayed Stadium. Just four days ago on October 19 at this exact Abu Dhabi venue, opener Sediqullah Atal struck a commanding 102 and leg-spinner Rashid Khan ripped through Zimbabwe with 4 for 17 in a 158-run demolition (294 to 136), giving Afghanistan decisive spin superiority on the run-equivalent handicap.

Take Danny Noppert to Win at -128 (1.78 fair decimal, 56.3% model probability) in Thursday's first-round clash against 28th seed Stephen Bunting in Dortmund. Official PDC schedule-of-play confirmation pits fifth seed Danny Noppert (£585,000 on the two-year PDC Order of Merit) directly against Bunting (£412,500) over a sprint best-of-11-legs format, where Noppert's superior European Tour floor consistency prices cleanly inside our focus band.

Side with Gerwyn Price to Win at -156 (1.64 fair decimal, 60.8% model probability) against Rob Cross in Westfalenhallen's best-of-11 opener. World #4 Gerwyn Price enters Dortmund carrying £782,000 on the official PDC Order of Merit — more than double #22 Rob Cross's £389,000 rolling tally — and four career European Championship final appearances underline Price's scoring comfort on the German stage.

Back Luke Littler -2.5 legs at -141 (1.71 fair decimal, 58.4% model probability) when World #1 Luke Littler faces #32 William O'Connor on Friday in Dortmund. Littler commands an astonishing £3,113,500 on the official PDC Order of Merit against O'Connor's £286,750, pushing Littler's outright win price well past -250 chalk; taking the standard -2.5 leg handicap captures his multi-break scoring power at an actionable price.

Back Hanwha Life Esports to Win at -137 (1.73 fair decimal, 57.7% model probability) over LPL #3 seed Top Esports in Friday's Swiss Round 1 marquee clash. Reigning MSI 2026 champions and LCK runners-up Hanwha Life Esports lean on star carries Zeka and Viper in late-game teamfights, holding a clear regional-seed and international-title edge over Top Esports (LPL Regional Finals #1) in a single-map opener.

Play Dplus KIA to Win at -156 (1.64 fair decimal, 61.1% model probability) in Friday's Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage Round 1 best-of-one at Credit Union of Texas Event Center. Even as LCK's fourth seed from Draw Pool 4, mid-laner ShowMaker and Dplus KIA bring battle-tested Korean macro discipline against Caps and LEC Summer champions G2 Esports, making the Korean representative a sharp in-band favorite on Riot's official Allen, Texas opening slate.
